site.title: Rust for TypeScript developers
site.description: An interactive Rust course for TypeScript developers. Learn ownership, borrowing and the type system side by side with the TypeScript you already write. Three tracks: basic, intermediate and advanced.

home.eyebrow: An interactive course for TypeScript developers
home.heroTitle: Learn Rust from the TypeScript you already write.
home.heroLead: You already know closures, generics, union types and async/await. This course starts from there and shows, side by side with TypeScript, what is actually different in Rust: ownership, the borrow checker, a stricter type system and a runtime that is almost nothing at all.
home.whyTitle: What changes when you come from TypeScript

why.title: No garbage collector
why.text: V8 frees memory for you, eventually. In Rust a value is freed deterministically when its owner goes out of scope. No GC pauses, no reference counting unless you ask for it.

why.title: Types that hold at runtime
why.text: No any, no null or undefined, no types erased before the code runs. Data races, use-after-free and missing values are rejected by the compiler, not discovered in production.

why.title: Zero-cost abstractions
why.text: Iterators, generics and closures compile ahead of time to the same machine code you would write by hand. No JIT, no warm-up.

why.title: Errors are values
why.text: No try/catch, no thrown values typed as unknown. Failure is part of the function signature through Result and Option.

home.tracksLead: Each track mixes concept explanations, diagrams and runnable examples. Every code block marked as a playground can be edited and executed in your browser. The basic track compares every concept with TypeScript; the later tracks also draw on other languages where it helps.
home.howText: Editable playgrounds are compiled and run on the official Rust Playground (play.rust-lang.org). Visualizations run entirely in your browser.
